I just cannot seem to find this but it seems so obvious I feel sure it must exist - is there (named) notation for the diagonal/codiagonal map into Prod/from Sum, a la https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diagonal_morphism - especially the former.

This is the map that sends a to (a, a)/the map that sends Sum.inl b -> b and Sum.inr -> b. In the latter case this is Sum.elim id id. I guess here I don't know the reverse, I think it is just composition with the constructors. What I suppose I am looking for is some kind of Prod.split or Prod.mkOf or something so that
Prod.mkOf id id is the map I want (and in general this would have type sig (f : γ → α) (g : γ → β ) : γ → α. We have this kind of thing as an equivalence in Mathlib (arrowProdEquivProdArrow, sumArrowEquivProdArrow). Notably in the former case, the reverse direction of this map is "composition with the destructors of Sum". So what I really want and what we don't seem to have notation for is a point-free way of expressing fun p c => (p.1 c, p.2 c).
I find this comes up a lot for me at all levels of Lean work, when I want to create a product which has each term dependent on a single input.
Yeah I think I feel we should have Prod.diag.
A canonical spelling would be nice I think
I'm sure I can whip up a PR. It really should be a core thing but maybe it can start in Mathlib.
